topic: The durable per-server_root_id identity contract

topic: MergeTreeData::Transaction::renameParts now commits every contract
canonical_claim: `MergeTreeData::Transaction::renameParts` now commits every part's disk-storage transaction before the Keeper commit decision, changing durability ordering for all `DiskObjectStorage`-backed MergeTree writes and requiring non-CA regression coverage before upstreaming. The required invariant is that a part is durable on its disk before its `block_id` and part-znode are registered in Keeper; parts-transaction commit only flips visibility, while rollback compensates with new operations over committed disk state. After `renameParts` returns, every part is durable at its final name; `Transaction::commit` only changes in-memory visibility, and rollback removes or compensates committed disk data. With the durability fix, a disk publish failure throws from `renameParts` before the Keeper multi, so no block-id znode exists and a retry inserts honestly. A crash between the Keeper multi and the later parts-transaction commit leaves the part durable at its final name, with a CA ref in the pool, so restart can see the part. If a later failure occurs after `renameParts`, rollback removes all preactive parts; published CA parts are reclaimed by ref removal and unpublished parts by temporary cleanup and destructor abandon, before any Keeper multi is reached. All audited `renameParts` call sites execute before an external commit decision or immediately before `commit` with no intervening decision, and paths bypassing it were found not to violate the durability invariant. The implementation closes each active part transaction in `renameParts` after deferred `renameTo`, while borrowed projection sub-parts do not independently commit because they share the parent's transaction. The generic durability invariant is that a part must be durably published before its Keeper block ID is registered; the proposed implementation closes the active disk transaction in `Transaction::renameParts` rather than adding CA-specific routing. The generic fix closes every part disk-storage transaction in `MergeTreeData::Transaction::renameParts` after deferred renames, with no CA-specific code change. The intended protocol is prepare durable and compensable storage before the Keeper decision, then apply visibility with a cheap finalize or compensate on abort; `renameParts` is the existing lock-free prepare slot. The agreed fix model closes the disk transaction at `renameParts`; a later parts-transaction commit has nothing left to do on disk, while rollback performs compensation as a new operation over committed state.

topic: namespaceIsRemoved gates its recreate-flip on the
canonical_claim: `namespaceIsRemoved` gates its recreate-flip on the `_cleanup` marker and `dropNamespace` publishes a constant-size `Removed` snapshot; both reader-side predicates must be re-derived from catalog state (`Removing`, then entry-absent) before the `_cleanup` marker class can be deleted.

topic: The writer no longer synchronizes a
canonical_claim: The writer no longer synchronizes a retired view or writer-side ack floor; it point-reads an add-only freshness meta at promote and copy-forward.

topic: The planned registry-free newborn protocol creates
canonical_claim: The planned registry-free newborn protocol creates a precommit-state shard fenced to the current `gcRound`, and gates `promote` on the shard's own `fence_round` rather than a registry fence.

topic: A first publish into a new
canonical_claim: A first publish into a new namespace uses the existing precommit machinery: the ref-shard becomes a precommit-state object, its `+1` is protected by the fold barrier, and there is no separate `pending-newborns` object.

topic: Phase 2 makes CachedPartFolderAccess the owner
canonical_claim: Phase 2 makes `CachedPartFolderAccess` the owner of freshness policy and terminal committed-ref primitives while `ContentAddressedMetadataStorage` retains path semantics and transactions retain staging orchestration.

topic: Write-through erases are cache hygiene rather
canonical_claim: Write-through erases are cache hygiene rather than a correctness dependency; `dropRefBestEffort` erases even when its underlying drop fails because durable ref state is then unknown.

topic: The two-level write API puts terminal
canonical_claim: The two-level write API puts terminal committed-ref primitives and `republishRef` in the facade, while `publishEntries` replaces the near-duplicate publish body of `adoptPartFromManifest` and transaction staging remains in the transaction.

topic: Writer cleanup removes stale precommit ownership
canonical_claim: Writer cleanup removes stale precommit ownership, and weak fairness of successor maintenance is expected to eventually clean pending stale ownership.

topic: Dead-precommit removal moved from GC to
canonical_claim: Dead-precommit removal moved from GC to the writer, which appends exact `owner_transition` removals; GC reclaims the resulting blobs through ordinary edge cancellation.

topic: Pool-member decommission performs full srid erasure
canonical_claim: Pool-member decommission performs full srid erasure of namespaces, manifest debris, staging, roots objects, and the slot, while subsequent normal GC rounds reclaim the now-unreferenced blob bytes.

topic: On atomic-write storages, VersionMetadataOnDisk writes version
canonical_claim: On atomic-write storages, `VersionMetadataOnDisk` writes version information with one `writeFile` instead of a temporary file plus rename.

topic: The freeze metadata_version_written_by_freeze special case is
canonical_claim: The freeze `metadata_version_written_by_freeze` special case is removed because an identical post-clone rewrite is absorbed by the byte-equal repoint no-op, while a differing rewrite may legally repoint.

topic: Pool/CasBlobUploader moves byte-delivery execution out of
canonical_claim: `Pool/CasBlobUploader` moves byte-delivery execution out of `CasBuild`, while admit/adopt/resurrect decisions and dependency-set recording remain on the transaction class.

topic: The proposed MOVE-to-CA fix is a
canonical_claim: The proposed MOVE-to-CA fix is a CAS-aware `clonePart` path that stages the whole part in one `ContentAddressedTransaction`; the generic per-file cross-disk copy path is insufficient.

topic: Whole-part atomicity sites such as freeze
canonical_claim: Whole-part atomicity sites such as `freeze`, restore-from-backup, and B58 projection commits remain single-`commit` transactions because this design deliberately introduces no `precommit` phase.

topic: Verbatim table-level and mountpoint files are
canonical_claim: Verbatim table-level and mountpoint files are treated as an immediate autocommit class: writes are durable on finalize and deletes or moves remain durable at call time, avoiding a second timeline for those files.

topic: The MOVE-to-CA design was reframed as
canonical_claim: The MOVE-to-CA design was reframed as one whole-part `ContentAddressedTransaction` threaded through the move, plus a layer-1 parser fix so the final part identity is used instead of `moving`; the earlier claim that a transactional copy would lack full build semantics was rejected.

topic: Review finding №12's call-time mutation of
canonical_claim: Review finding №12's call-time mutation of durable refs is by design: `renameParts` is the commit point and rollback compensates with new operations over committed disk state, but `removeDirectory` must discard staged entries when removing a part before commit.

topic: For CA part moves, the crash-atomic
canonical_claim: For CA part moves, the crash-atomic design uses a transient `moving/<part>` reference prefix: `clonePart` commits under the moving reference and the mover later repoints it to the final reference, so startup cleanup can reclaim an orphaned moving reference.

topic: The production INSERT topology contract
canonical_claim: The production INSERT topology commits one `ContentAddressedTransaction` per part, so cross-part batching must occur at the `MergeTreeData::Transaction::renameParts` seam rather than inside `ContentAddressedTransaction::commit`. A plain INSERT performs one `ContentAddressedTransaction::commit()` per part with `parts.size() == 1`, so inner-loop parallelism cannot improve INSERT; cross-part concurrency must be introduced above the disk transaction.

topic: The phased engine uses one precommit
canonical_claim: The phased engine uses one precommit ledger batch, one flattened cross-part upload wave, and one promote ledger batch; a 500-part INSERT is expected to reduce about 1026 serial ref-log PUTs to about two.

topic: The approved inner-loop design dispatches each
canonical_claim: The approved inner-loop design dispatches each part's unchanged `stageManifest → precommitAdd → uploadPendingBlobs → promote` sequence to bounded workers, preserving per-part ordering while overlapping parts.

topic: The CAS commit pool must use
canonical_claim: The CAS commit pool must use bounded worker-loop callbacks or a dedicated pool sized by `cas_commit_concurrency`; scheduling one task per part on a shared 100-thread pool would not enforce the bound and could starve unrelated users.

topic: The initial multi-commit design used commitTransactions
canonical_claim: The initial multi-commit design used `commitTransactions` as a transaction-centric seam: generic implementations loop sequentially, while `MergeTreeData::Transaction::renameParts` groups same-disk transactions without leaking `isContentAddressed` checks into generic MergeTree code.

topic: Move assignment for PreparedPartWrite is deleted
canonical_claim: Move assignment for `PreparedPartWrite` is deleted because overwriting a handle that still owes a terminal action may require a fallible `abandon`, which move assignment cannot report without dropping cleanup ownership.

topic: The part-write release seam is relink-independent
canonical_claim: The part-write release seam is relink-independent: any `PartWriteTxn` may leave a staged precommit whose release is unproven, and the accounting is intentionally not attributed to relink or another consumer.

topic: ~PartWriteTxn, rather than ~PreparedPartWrite, owns the
canonical_claim: `~PartWriteTxn`, rather than `~PreparedPartWrite`, owns the final release word because `prepareEntries` can fail before constructing a handle; the transaction destructor therefore covers both handle and no-handle staging exits.

topic: Poisoned is not equivalent to a
canonical_claim: `Poisoned` is not equivalent to a wedge: it means a durable transaction may be missing from the cached view, so it continues to block snapshot publication and triggers re-recovery; making `ApplyPending` debug-only is a follow-up, not part of Stage B.

topic: The RemovalReady protocol is adopted as
canonical_claim: The `RemovalReady` protocol is adopted as a transient catalog state between `Removing` and entry deletion: it is entered only after the terminal record has folded and the life-scoped cleanup item is durably `Completed`.

topic: The final recommendation is to keep
canonical_claim: The final recommendation is to keep `NamespaceLifeId` and incarnation-qualified ref and namespace-file keys, avoid permanent `Retired` history and extra retirement markers, and delete a catalog entry only after terminal fold, cleanup/cursor retirement, and exact `_ckpt` deletion ordering is complete.

topic: The incarnation is retained because temporary
canonical_claim: The incarnation is retained because temporary refusal alone cannot make omitted old physical objects safe for eventual same-name reuse; the generation makes old ref objects and namespace files structurally inert.

topic: The RemovalReady state machine is Creating
canonical_claim: The `RemovalReady` state machine is `Creating -> Live -> Removing -> RemovalReady -> absent`; `RemovalReady` means no writer publication, recovery, ref fold, or new cursor is permitted, and only exact removal of the row is legal.

topic: Build::abandon must call retireBuildSeq only after
canonical_claim: `Build::abandon` must call `retireBuildSeq` only after the precommit-removal `mutateShard`, so the build becomes watermark-dead only after its removal is durable; this ordering mirrors `Build::promote`.

topic: The tokenless DETACH/freeze adopt path can
canonical_claim: The tokenless DETACH/freeze adopt path can race GC condemnation because `copyForwardFromCondemned` runs once before the CAS closure; the proposed fix is a bounded copy-forward and re-HEAD loop outside the closure, analogous to tokened resurrection.
